authoritative_rubric.text: sex_reporting: 3 if sex comparison is the primary aim and a sex result is reported, 2 for any explicit sex-stratified outcome or sex interaction test, including a null interaction, or 1 for demographics only if reviewing the full article. Return null if only the abstract is provided and no qualifying outcome is shown. In the full article, use 0 if a quoted analysis passage explicitly establishes pooling or sex adjustment alone; return null if absence is unclear. Demographics and adjustment alone are not sex-disaggregated outcomes.

coding_definitions.level_0: No sex reporting at all, or pooled/non-sex-specific reporting only. Assigned only from a full article where a quoted analysis passage explicitly establishes pooling or sex adjustment alone.
coding_definitions.level_1: Participant sex reported demographically (sample composition, sex-matched groups, counts) but no sex-stratified outcome, no sex interaction/moderation test, and adjustment alone kept below the disaggregation threshold. Per the rubric, level 1 requires reviewing the full article.
coding_definitions.level_2: Explicit sex-stratified outcome, sex as a predictor with an outcome effect estimate, or bivariate outcome comparison by sex, with no formal interaction/moderation test.
coding_definitions.level_3: Formal statistical test of sex differences/interaction/moderation (including null interactions), or sex comparison as the primary aim with a reported result.
coding_definitions.unresolved: Only the abstract is available and it shows no qualifying sex outcome; the rubric requires null (unresolved) rather than a speculative 0 or 1.

key_distinctions: Reporting participant sex (demographics) is not the same as adjusting for sex in a model; adjustment alone is below the level-2 threshold.
Level 1 (demographics only) requires full-article review; abstract-only demographic mentions remain unresolved.
Level 2 vs 3: a sex effect estimate or stratified reporting = 2; a formal interaction/moderation test (even null) = 3.
Do not infer that no sex analysis occurred merely because an abstract omits it; document an evidence gap instead.
